Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how Alderbridge Care Group recognises a staff member's long service. It applies
to every permanent member of staff across every site.

Policy statement

Long service is recognised meaningfully at defined milestones, reflecting the genuine value of experienced
staff who have chosen to build their career at Alderbridge.

Definitions

**Milestone year** a service anniversary of 5, 10, 15 or 20 years, at which a specific recognition is given.
**Continuous service** service counted without a break exceeding the threshold set out in the Staff
Handbook, used to determine milestone eligibility.

1. HR identifies an upcoming milestone anniversary from payroll records and notifies the site three months
in advance.

2. Present recognition at a team meeting or similar site event, marking the milestone visibly rather than
only administratively.

3. Award a certificate at every milestone, with an additional day of annual leave awarded from the 10-year
milestone onward and a cash award from the 15-year milestone onward.

4. Record the recognition given in the staff member's personnel file.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a staff member has had a single approved career break (such as extended parental leave) that

Appendix: the nine protected characteristics in an Alderbridge context

This appendix illustrates, for training purposes, how each of the Equality Act 2010's nine protected characteristics shows up in practice at Alderbridge, expanding on the Definitions section above. Age is relevant both to older residents and to younger staff or job applicants, and this policy applies equally in both directions — an assumption that an older applicant is 'less tech-savvy' is treated exactly as seriously as an assumption that a younger applicant is 'not ready for responsibility.' Disability covers both staff with a disability needing a reasonable adjustment and residents whose care needs stem from a disability, which this policy treats as a dignity matter, not solely a clinical one. Gender reassignment is relevant to staff and, occasionally, to residents or their family members, and Alderbridge uses a person's own stated name and pronouns consistently across every record and conversation. Marriage and civil partnership status is never a factor in a recruitment, promotion or care decision. Pregnancy and maternity are protected from the point Alderbridge is told about a pregnancy, addressed specifically in the risk-assessment section of the Health and Safety Policy Statement. Race, religion or belief, sex, and sexual orientation are each protected in recruitment, employment and care delivery alike, and a resident's own view is never used to justify discriminatory treatment of a member of staff on any of these grounds, even where the resident's view reflects a genuinely held but discriminatory personal belief.

Alderbridge deliberately employs across a wide age range, from school-leaver apprentices to staff working well past the state pension age, and rota and physical-task planning takes genuine account of individual capability rather than age itself, since age alone is never used as a proxy for what tasks someone can safely undertake in either direction.

Marriage, civil partnership and family status

Decisions about shift patterns, promotion or opportunity are never influenced by whether an employee is married, in a civil partnership, or has caring responsibilities of their own, and a request for flexibility linked to family circumstances is considered under the Flexible Working Policy on its own merits rather than viewed less favourably because of an assumption about where an employee's priorities lie.

Appendix: raising a concern under this policy, step by step

This appendix sets out, in plain terms, the practical steps for someone experiencing or witnessing a breach of this policy. Speak to your line manager, or HR directly if the concern involves your line manager, as the first step in most cases. If informal action does not resolve it, raise a formal grievance under the Grievance Procedure, or report it for investigation under the Disciplinary Procedure if you are reporting someone else's conduct rather than raising your own grievance. Keep a note of what happened, when, and who else was present or aware, since this helps any investigation establish the facts clearly. Ask for support from a trade union representative or colleague at any formal stage — this right exists specifically to make raising a difficult concern less daunting. Expect to be kept informed of progress and given reasons for the eventual outcome, whichever process is used.

Contractors and agency workers

Contractors and agency workers are held to the same standard of conduct under this policy as directly employed staff while working at an Alderbridge site, and a concern about a contractor's or agency worker's conduct is investigated by the registered manager in the same way as for an employee, with the outcome fed back to that person's own employer or agency where the finding warrants it, including a request that they not return to an Alderbridge site if appropriate.

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out Alderbridge Care Group's commitment to equality of opportunity and to a working and caring environment free of discrimination, harassment and victimisation. It applies to staff, job applicants, people supported, and anyone Alderbridge interacts with, in line with the Equality Act 2010 and its nine protected characteristics: age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, and sexual orientation.

Policy statement

Alderbridge believes that dignity is not a separate, optional layer on top of good care and good employment practice, but the thing both are ultimately for. This policy is treated as being as central to Alderbridge's culture as any clinical or financial standard.

Definitions

**Direct discrimination** treating someone less favourably because of a protected characteristic. **Indirect discrimination** applying a rule or practice that disadvantages people with a protected characteristic without objective justification. **Harassment** unwanted conduct related to a protected characteristic that violates someone's dignity or creates an intimidating, hostile, degrading, humiliating or offensive environment. **Victimisation** treating someone unfairly because they have made or supported a complaint about discrimination. **Reasonable adjustment** a change to a workplace or recruitment process, or to how care is delivered, to remove a disadvantage a disabled person would otherwise face.

Roles and responsibilities

**Every manager** models inclusive behaviour and addresses concerns raised to them promptly, rather than treating equality as someone else's specialist responsibility. **HR** advises on reasonable adjustments and investigates any complaint alleging discrimination or harassment, working alongside the Grievance Procedure or Disciplinary Procedure as appropriate. **The registered manager** ensures care delivery itself reflects individual cultural, religious and personal preference wherever practicable, recorded in each person's care plan.

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out Alderbridge Care Group's commitment to equality of opportunity and to a working and caring environment free of discrimination, harassment and victimisation. Policy statement

Policy statement

brought into use because it seemed useful. **Every member of staff using a hazardous substance**
follows the SDS's PPE and handling requirements without exception.

Data Protection Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group meets its obligations under the UK GDPR and Data
Protection Act 2018 when processing personal data about people supported, staff, job applicants, and
anyone else whose data Alderbridge holds. It applies to every site, every system, and every format
personal data is held in, whether digital, paper, photographic or verbal, and to every member of staff,
volunteer, contractor and agency worker with any access to it.

Policy statement

Alderbridge treats personal data, and in particular the special category health and care data it holds about
people supported, as something staff are trusted with rather than something they are simply permitted to
use. A breach of this policy is taken as seriously as a breach of any safeguarding or medication standard,
because a data breach involving a vulnerable person's health information can itself cause real, lasting
harm.

Definitions

**Personal data** any information relating to an identified or identifiable living person. **Special category
data** personal data revealing health, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation or similar, subject to stricter
conditions for processing. **Data controller** the organisation (Alderbridge) that decides why and how
personal data is processed. **Data processor** a third party (for example, a payroll provider) processing
personal data on Alderbridge's behalf under a contract. **Lawful basis** the specific legal ground under
UK GDPR Article 6 (and, for special category data, Article 9) that justifies a particular processing activity.
**Data subject** the individual the personal data is about.

Purpose and scope

Outbreak Management Procedure

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group declares, manages and closes an infectious disease outbreak at any of its sites. It applies to every site and covers respiratory, gastrointestinal and other transmissible infections, working alongside the wider infection prevention and control framework the Hand Hygiene Policy and PPE Guidance establish for everyday practice.

Policy statement

An outbreak in a communal care setting spreads faster and affects more vulnerable people than in almost any other environment, and Alderbridge treats early, decisive action as protecting residents' health first and their normal social and family life second — never the reverse, but also never sustaining a restriction for longer than the evidence genuinely requires.

Definitions

**Outbreak** two or more people supported or staff at the same site developing symptoms of the same suspected infection within 48 hours. **Incubation period** the time between exposure to an infectious agent and the appearance of symptoms, used to determine how long an outbreak's control measures must continue after the last new case. **Enhanced cleaning** an increased frequency and intensity of cleaning specific to the suspected pathogen, beyond the site's everyday standard. **Cohorting** grouping affected and unaffected people, and where practicable staff, separately to limit further transmission.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager** declares an outbreak, notifies the local Health Protection Team and the Alderbridge Quality Lead, and leads the site's own outbreak response. **Every member of staff** reports any new suspected case immediately and follows the enhanced cleaning and PPE requirements without exception once an outbreak is declared. **The Alderbridge Quality Lead** coordinates any cross-site implication (for example, a staff member who has worked shifts at two sites during the incubation period) and reports outbreak activity to the Board.

On identifying a second case of the same suspected infection within 48 hours of the first, the registered manager declares an outbreak and notifies the local Health Protection Team the same day.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out the waking check standard for night staff at Alderbridge Care Group. It applies to every site running an overnight shift.

Policy statement

Every resident is checked by night staff at intervals of no more than 2 hours, or more often if their individual care plan says so, balancing a resident's need for undisturbed sleep with the safety benefit of a regular check.

Definitions

**Waking check** a check where the staff member confirms the resident's wellbeing sufficiently to be satisfied they are safe, without necessarily fully waking a sleeping resident unnecessarily. **Individual care plan interval** a shorter interval than the standard 2 hours, specified for a resident whose needs require more frequent checking.

Roles and responsibilities

**Night staff** check every resident at intervals of no more than 2 hours, recording each check. **The registered nurse or senior carer** sets an individual care plan interval for a resident whose needs require more frequent checking. **The registered manager** reviews waking check records as part of routine night-shift oversight.

1. Check every resident at intervals of no more than 2 hours through the night.
2. Follow a shorter, individually specified interval where a resident's care plan says so.
3. Record each check at the time it is completed, not retrospectively at the end of the shift.
4. Escalate immediately to the registered nurse or on-call manager if a check reveals a concern.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Duty of Candour: What Staff Need to Know

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how Alderbridge Care Group meets its duty of candour when a notifiable safety incident occurs. It applies to every site and every member of staff involved in a resident's care.

Policy statement

Alderbridge is open and honest with a resident and their family when something has gone wrong in their care, explaining what happened, apologising genuinely, and setting out what will be done in response, because this openness is both a regulatory duty and simply the right thing to do.

Definitions

**Duty of candour** the statutory and professional duty to be open and transparent with a resident or their representative when a notifiable safety incident occurs. **Notifiable safety incident** an unintended or unexpected incident that resulted in, or could have resulted in, death or significant harm. **Reasonable apology** a genuine, meaningful apology for what happened, not a legal admission of liability.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager** identifies whether an incident meets the notifiable threshold and leads the duty of candour conversation, or delegates this to a suitably senior colleague. **Care staff** report any incident that might meet the threshold promptly, without deciding themselves that it does not qualify. **The Quality Lead** supports the registered manager in preparing the written notification that follows the initial conversation.

Welcome to Alderbridge

Alderbridge aims to make every resident feel genuinely at home, supported to live with dignity, independence and real choice.

A resident is encouraged to personalise their room with familiar belongings, photographs and furniture where practicable.

Each site runs a weekly activities programme shaped by resident preference.

Moving and Handling Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group protects staff, and the people they support, from the risk of injury during moving and handling activities — assisting a person to stand, transfer, reposition, or move using equipment such as a hoist or slide sheet. It applies to every member of staff involved in any moving and handling activity at any site, and to the equipment provided to support it.

Policy statement

Manual handling injury is one of the most common and most preventable causes of staff injury in social care, and Alderbridge treats prevention as a matter of training, equipment and individual risk assessment working together, never as something staff are simply expected to manage through personal caution or physical strength alone.

Definitions

**Moving and handling risk assessment (MHRA)** the individual, written assessment completed for every person supported who needs any level of physical assistance to move, specifying exactly what equipment and technique must be used. **Hoist** powered equipment used to lift a person who cannot bear weight or transfer independently. **Slide sheet** low-friction fabric used to reposition a person in bed with minimal physical effort. **Two-person assist** a moving and handling technique requiring two trained staff working together, specified where a single-person technique would be unsafe. **Ceiling track hoist** a fixed hoist system installed in a room, used where a mobile hoist would be impractical.

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out Alderbridge Care Group's commitment to equality of opportunity and to a working and caring environment free of discrimination, harassment and victimisation. Appendix: the 72-hour clock at a glance

For quick reference: the clock starts when Alderbridge becomes aware of the breach, not when the
investigation concludes; internal reporting within 1 hour of discovery gives the Data Protection Lead the
maximum possible time within that window to investigate properly and, where required, notify the ICO with
a genuinely complete, accurate assessment rather than a rushed, incomplete one submitted only to beat
the deadline.

but the Data Protection Lead also proactively checks in with key processors periodically, since the 72-hour
clock for Alderbridge's own notification obligation still runs from when Alderbridge itself becomes aware,
which can be later than when the processor's own breach actually occurred if the processor is slow to tell
Alderbridge.

applies in full; a former employee's data remains protected personal data for as long as Alderbridge holds

rather than an external party?** No — an internal misdirection can still be a genuine breach, particularly for
special category health data, and is assessed on the actual risk to the individual concerned, not assumed
low risk purely because it stayed within the organisation. **Is a physical break-in and theft of paper records
treated the same as a digital breach?** Yes — the same assessment and notification process applies
regardless of whether the compromised data was digital or physical.

Policy statement

Long service is recognised meaningfully at defined milestones, reflecting the genuine value of experienced
